reviews.one_line_contribution: A token-matched and format-matched control for agentic experience memory showing the per-query read is inert -- correctly retrieved top-k (A1(7)) buys no more than decoys retrieved for a different query (A2(7)) or a single fixed prefix identical across all queries (A3(7)), and no more than a bank compiled offline into one instruction (P1) -- with a measured experience-following rate to establish that the injected text is read yet valueless, rather than ignored.
reviews.closest_prior_work: The threat the proposal never names is the in-context-learning demonstration-selection literature, not the agentic-memory literature it surveys. Min et al. 2022 ('Rethinking the Role of Demonstrations') is the same dissociation the proposal calls its centerpiece: models condition on demonstration format and input distribution while the correctness of the demonstration content contributes little, i.e. following without benefit. Cuconasu et al. 2024 ('The Power of Noise') is the same decoy arm: random/irrelevant retrieved passages substituted at matched count do not degrade, and can improve, RAG accuracy. Liu et al. 2022 and the retrieval-vs-random exemplar comparisons that followed made 'retrieved-for-this-query vs random-at-equal-k' a standard ICL protocol years ago. That does not fully preempt the proposal -- self-collected multi-step trajectories in a sequential environment are a different object from labeled QA exemplars, Yoo et al. 2022 showed Min et al.'s null weakens with scale and task type, and A3(7)'s prefix-cacheability argument is genuinely new -- but it converts the contribution from 'a control nobody has run' to 'a known ICL control transplanted to agent memory,' which is a much smaller claim than the abstract makes. On the constructive side Atlas (arXiv:2603.15666) and Dynamic Cheatsheet (arXiv:2504.07952) already own compilation-as-method, and the proposal correctly concedes this; the residual novelty is entirely in the A1/A2/A3 conditioning block and the ExpeL B1-B5 decomposition.
reviews.strongest_objection: The conditioning claim is likely vacuous by construction, and nothing in the pre-registration prevents it. This track's own prior measured result is that injecting seven retrieved items fixed zero instances and broke six to seven (McNemar p=0.031 and p=0.016, replicated), and that cutting seven to three removed the harm. The proposal then makes k=7 the load-bearing configuration for predictions 1-3. If A1(7) does not beat A0 above the measured noise floor -- which the track's own pilot says is the expected outcome at exactly this k -- then A1(7) ~ A2(7) ~ A3(7) demonstrates only that three ways of adding useless tokens are equally useless. The paper would then be entitled to say 'the memory channel is inert at 14B,' a weaker and partly already-reported claim, but not 'the query-conditioning is inert,' which requires there to be something for conditioning to have been responsible for. Prediction 1's own escape clause exposes this: 'at least 80% of whatever advantage correct retrieval holds over A0 survives replacement by decoys' is a ratio whose denominator (A1(7) - A0) is expected to be zero or negative, making the criterion undefined rather than lenient. Prediction 7 does not patch the hole, because it gates on P1 - P0 (the compiled bank beating bank-blind optimization), not on the injected bank ever having worked. Compounding this, the pre-registered TOST margin of +/-3 points on WebShop is the same magnitude as the gains ExpeL, AWM and A-Mem report; passing equivalence at +/-3 bounds the retrieval channel at roughly the size its advocates already claim for it, so the headline 'ExpeL's ablation row should not survive a token-matched control' is not licensed by the test as specified.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: (1) Pre-register a positive-control gate: the conditioning claim is reported only if A1(7) - A0 (or, failing that, A5 - A0) exceeds the 95th-percentile null-replicate floor in that environment; otherwise the paper reports 'the injected memory channel is inert at this scale' and drops the conditioning framing, exactly as it already commits to do for the P1 ~ P0 case. Relatedly, run the conditioning block at the dev-tuned k* rather than fixing k=7, so the retrieval arm is evaluated at its best configuration and not at the value this track already measured as harmful. (2) Tighten the equivalence margin to below the effect sizes the target papers claim -- roughly +/-0.015 WebShop reward and +/-2 points EM -- and re-derive n, or state explicitly in the abstract that the result bounds the channel at, not below, the published claim sizes. Note also that applying Holm across the ten-row conditioning family to TOST tests inflates the effective margin further and needs to be handled explicitly. (3) Add the missing arm below. (4) Add a single 32B point (the track budget explicitly allows ~32B on 4xA100); with only 8B and 14B, 'conditioning becomes useful at frontier scale' is not merely unexcluded, it is the reviewer's default reading. (5) Cite and position against Min et al. 2022 and Cuconasu et al. 2024; the gap statement is currently a claim about the agentic-memory subfield being unaware of a control that ICL has run for years.
reviews.missing_baseline: P1 + live top-k retrieval at inference: the compiled, bank-derived instruction held fixed with the retrieval channel simply switched on. This is what a practitioner does when adding memory to an already-optimized prompt, and it is the only clean test of 'retrieval adds nothing on top of compilation.' As specified, P2 vs P1 confounds the channel with a differently-optimized instruction (P2's instruction was evolved against retrieval, P1's was not), and P2 vs P3 holds the instruction fixed but only swaps content, never removes it -- so no contrast in the grid isolates the marginal value of retrieval given a compiled instruction. It costs 500 additional episodes. Secondary omissions a reviewer would also press: an A1 arm at the dev-tuned k* alongside A1(7), and one open-weight model above 14B.
reviews.preprint_collision: This is a better-than-average check -- nine queries, a named hard collision (Atlas, arXiv:2603.15666) with an argued and falsifiable distinction, a named counter-hypothesis (arXiv:2606.06036), and an explicit correction retracting prior-round citations -- but it undercuts itself in two specific ways. First, it discloses that five citations load-bearing in the previous round (MemHarness 2607.28272, RecMem 2605.16045, AtomicRAG 2604.20844, Distractor-Aware Truncation 2608.03297, and 'Decocted Experience' 2604.04373, previously flagged as the closest threat) could not be re-found this round and were removed. A search instrument whose returns do not replicate between rounds cannot support a gap statement, and the current round's unverified items -- Auto-Dreamer 2605.20616, Structured Distillation 2603.13017, and Atlas itself, whose venue and authorship the author admits could not be confirmed -- inherit exactly that doubt. The honest reading is that the sole named hard collision may be a mirage in either direction, and the proposal cannot presently tell which. Second, and more damagingly, all nine queries appear to be phrased over agentic memory; none searched the ICL demonstration-selection space (retrieved vs random exemplars at matched k, ground-truth-label ablations), which is where the predicted null is closest to already-established. I did not find a preprint that runs the exact A1/A2/A3 grid inside a published agentic-memory system, so predictions 1-3 and 6 are probably still open; but the gap statement as written overclaims, because it establishes only that one subfield has not run a control that a neighboring subfield made routine.

reviews.one_line_contribution: A token-matched and format-matched control set (correct top-k vs. off-query decoys vs. one fixed prefix vs. an offline-compiled instruction) applied to agentic experience memory, paired with a measured experience-following rate, to argue that the per-query conditioning step contributes zero while the bank still contributes query-independently.
reviews.closest_prior_work: The proposal's own list is not the real threat; the threat is the in-context-learning demonstration-selection literature it never cites. Min et al. 2022 (Rethinking the Role of Demonstrations) established the template argument -- swap the semantically correct content of demonstrations for mismatched content at fixed format and fixed count, observe no accuracy loss, and conclude the model is reading format and distribution rather than the query-specific payload -- and Yoo et al. 2022 and the Z-ICL line refined it. The counterweight, Liu et al. 2022 (KATE / What Makes Good In-Context Examples for GPT-3), showed retrieval-based selection does beat random selection, and the subsequent literature has repeatedly found the gain small and dataset-dependent. Predictions 1-3 are that decade-old ablation ported from static classification ICL to agentic trajectories, and an area chair will ask what is conceptually new beyond the port. The proposal can answer that -- agentic memory items are procedures used over multi-step rollouts, not label-bearing exemplars, and no one has run the swap inside a deployed agent memory stack -- but it does not answer it, because it never notices the literature. Within its own list, ExpeL (arXiv:2308.10144) threatens least (it contains the insight/trajectory split but not the token-matched swap) and Dynamic Cheatsheet (arXiv:2504.07952) plus the claimed Atlas (arXiv:2603.15666) threaten only the compilation half, which the proposal correctly concedes.
reviews.strongest_objection: There is no pre-registered gate requiring the retrieval channel to be worth anything before its query-conditioning is declared inert, and the track's own prior measurement makes the ungated world the likely one. The brief this proposal answers reports that injecting seven retrieved items fixed zero items and broke six to seven (McNemar p=0.031, p=0.016, replicated), and that cutting to three items eliminated the harm. The centerpiece then makes A1(7) the canonical read and builds every equivalence claim on it. If A1(7) - A0 is at or below zero on WebShop, prediction 1 is satisfied trivially: decoys match correct retrieval because neither is worth anything, and the paper has shown that a channel with no value has no query-specific value -- which is the track's already-published result restated with more conditions. Prediction 1's own escape hatch, the 'at least 80 percent of whatever advantage correct retrieval holds over A0 survives replacement' formulation, is undefined when the denominator is near zero or negative, and no inference procedure or minimum denominator is pre-registered for that ratio. The guard against this is A5, the oracle nearest-gold trajectory, which the Risk section explicitly names as the arm that decides whether the finding generalizes -- yet A5 sits in the supporting tier at one seed with no null replicate, no MDE, and no TOST margin. The single arm that determines which paper this is is the least powered one in the grid. Compounding this, the only contrast that overturns a published result is prediction 6 on ALFWorld (B1 vs. B2, B4, B5), and the Measurement section states in plain words that ALFWorld at n approximately 234 cannot support equivalence claims (MDE 7-8 points). Prediction 6 is an equivalence claim on ALFWorld. The proposal contradicts itself on its own headline consequence: the powered environments have no published claim to overturn, and the environment with the published claim to overturn is conceded to be unable to support the test.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: Four changes, none expensive. (1) Pre-register an interpretability gate: state the minimum A1(7) - A0 and A5 - A0 above the measured noise floor below which the equivalence claims are reported as uninformative rather than as support for inertness, and commit to that reframing in advance the way risk 3 already commits for P1 approximately equal to P0. (2) Promote A5 and A6 into the decisive set at two seeds with their own null replicates and MDEs; the oracle is not a supporting curiosity, it is the denominator of the entire claim. (3) Move prediction 6 off ALFWorld or drop the equivalence language there. Either pool the seen and unseen splits into a single larger ALFWorld evaluation, or port the B1-B5 decomposition onto WebShop and E3 using an ExpeL-style write path so the ExpeL logic is tested where the power lives, and let n approximately 234 ALFWorld carry direction only, exactly as the Measurement section says it must. (4) Strengthen the decoy. A2(7) drawn from a disjoint task family is the easy negative; add hard negatives drawn from ranks 24-30 of A6's own 30-candidate pool for the current query -- same topic, same environment, same format, wrong ranking -- so the claim separates 'ranking quality is inert' from the much weaker 'topical relevance is inert'. Also state whether the TOST tests are themselves Holm-corrected across the ten-row conditioning family; if they are, the stated MDE of 0.031 reward at a TOST margin of 0.03 no longer delivers the advertised power, and the margins or n need revising.
reviews.missing_baseline: Two, plus one symmetry gap. First, the entire conditioning block at k=3: A2(3) and A3(3) do not exist anywhere in the grid, and A1(3) is demoted to supporting at one seed. The track's own prior work identified k=3 as the injection budget at which memory stops being harmful, which makes it the operating point where conditioning has the best chance of showing value -- each item carries more weight, distraction is minimal, and there is no seven-item length penalty to swamp the signal. Testing conditioning only at the budget already known to be harmful stacks the deck toward the null. Second, hard-negative decoys from the same query's own candidate pool (see above); without them the result reads as 'off-topic text is ignorable', which is unsurprising, rather than 'ranking within topic is worthless', which is the interesting claim. The symmetry gap: A2u swaps in a foreign environment's bank at retrieval time, but there is no P1u that compiles a foreign environment's bank into an instruction. P0 (bank-blind) bounds compilation from one side only; P1u would test whether P1's gain over P0 is bank-specific content or merely more agent-flavored instruction text, which is what prediction 7 actually needs.
reviews.preprint_collision: Procedurally this is among the better collision checks one sees -- nine queries, two collisions named rather than buried, a live counter-hypothesis (arXiv:2606.06036) reported as a threat to significance, an explicit statement that the gap claim is a claim about the search and not proof of absence, and a named consequence if the Atlas group adds a decoy arm. Substantively it is much weaker than it looks, and the proposal itself supplies the reason. The 'Correction carried forward' paragraph concedes that the previous round cited five items (MemHarness 2607.28272, RecMem 2605.16045, AtomicRAG 2604.20844, Distractor-Aware Truncation 2608.03297, and a retitled 2606.06036) that this round's search could not re-verify, and that arXiv:2604.04373, previously flagged as the closest threat, did not reappear at all. The same retrieval apparatus produced this round's eight items, and the author admits verifying Atlas only from an introduction snippet with no confirmed venue or authorship. So the load-bearing collision -- the one that determines whether the compilation half is preempted -- rests on an unverified artifact, and the honest inference is that the current eight need independent confirmation (title, authors, abstract, ablation table) before novelty can be granted on their basis. Of the cited set I can vouch for ExpeL (2308.10144), AWM (2409.07429), and Dynamic Cheatsheet (2504.07952); the 2603-2608 identifiers I cannot. Separately, the search's scope is too narrow to establish the novelty claimed: every query appears to sit inside agentic memory, so it could not have surfaced the ICL demonstration-selection line (Min et al. 2022, Liu et al. 2022, Yoo et al. 2022) where mismatched-content and random-selection controls at fixed format are routine methodology. An unsearched adjacent literature that already runs your central ablation in a neighboring setting is a novelty problem, not a neutral, and it is the one this check missed.

reviews.one_line_contribution: A token- and format-matched control the agentic-memory literature never runs: replacing per-query retrieved experience with decoys, with a single dev-selected fixed prefix, or with an offline-compiled instruction, and showing accuracy is statistically unchanged while the agent still demonstrably imitates the injected items — i.e., the read channel's query-conditioning, not just its volume, is inert.
reviews.closest_prior_work: Atlas (arXiv:2603.15666) is the nearest and the proposal is right that it builds the replacement (compile experience into the system prompt) without showing the replaced channel contributed zero; the residual delta is therefore a single contrast, correct-vs-decoy/fixed-prefix at matched tokens. The under-treated threat is Dynamic Cheatsheet (arXiv:2504.07952), which already runs one persistent cross-query artifact against per-item retrieval; the proposal dismisses it in one clause ('presented as a method with its own gains') without saying whether its ablations already include a token-comparable per-query-retrieval arm — if they do, prediction 4 is largely pre-empted and only predictions 1-3 survive. arXiv:2505.16067 further shows retrieved experience is often followed and sometimes harmful, so 'retrieval does not help' is already partly on the record; what is new is only 'correct is worth no more than decoy at matched tokens, with following held high'.
reviews.strongest_objection: The decisive grid is centred on A1(7), a budget the proposal's own research track already measured as net harmful (7 retrieved items fixed zero and broke six to seven, McNemar p=0.031/0.016; cutting to three eliminated the harm). If A1(7) is at or below A0, then A1(7)-A2(7) and A1(7)-A3(7) are equivalence tests between two treatments that do not work, and prediction 1's '>=80% of whatever advantage correct retrieval holds over A0 survives' is undefined rather than confirmed. The one arm at the budget where retrieval plausibly helps, A1(3), is demoted to the 1-seed supporting set and has no matched counterparts — there is no A2(3) and no A3(3) — so the central claim cannot be evaluated at k=3 at all. Compounding this, the environments are chosen where a query-independent prior is near-sufficient by construction (WebShop's action grammar and ALFWorld's task templates are shared across queries; a decoy from a 'different task family' still demonstrates search[...]/click[Buy Now]), so a null is close to a foregone conclusion and does not license the general claim that query-conditioning is inert. The design's own guard against that triviality — A5 (oracle nearest-gold) and A2u — sits in the 1-seed supporting tier with no null replicate, i.e. the arms that decide whether the headline is a real finding or 'our bank had no exploitable content' are the least powered arms in the paper. Risk factor 5 names this exact failure and then does not resource it.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: (1) Make A1(k*) - A0 > equivalence margin a stated gate, exactly parallel to the ExpeL fidelity gate: if correct retrieval does not beat no-memory by more than +/-3 reward points, report that and stop, because every downstream equivalence claim is vacuous. (2) Run the full conditioning triplet at both budgets — A1(3)/A2(3)/A3(3) as well as k=7 — with 2 seeds each, so the claim is not confined to a budget already known to be over-injected. (3) Promote A5 and A2u into the decisive set with null replicates; a flat oracle should be reported as 'bank had no headroom', not as support for inertness. (4) Add one environment where the bank contains information not recoverable from the query itself (site-specific quirks, tool-schema exceptions, cross-episode facts) so that a bank with demonstrated conditioning headroom exists somewhere in the paper; without it the title claim outruns the evidence. (5) Fix the offline-compute arithmetic: '~20 iterations against a 300-episode dev split' totalling 3,300 dev episodes across 11 GEPA runs implies ~15 episodes per candidate evaluation, far below the paper's own 5-14 point re-scoring drift, so P2's 'plateau' curve cannot distinguish convergence from noise and predictions 4-5 inherit that.
reviews.missing_baseline: A sham/counterfactual following-rate baseline: score A0 (no-memory) episodes against the items that would have been retrieved, using the identical n-gram/entity/LLM-judge pipeline. Prediction 3 — the dissociation that the abstract calls the core evidence — is uninterpretable without it, because in WebShop and ALFWorld the action vocabulary is tiny and correct items share entity strings with the query, so 'following' is measured with an upward bias on A1 and a downward bias on A2/A3; a decoy following rate at 70% of the correct rate could be entirely chance overlap, and equally a low decoy rate could be metric artifact rather than the agent ignoring the text. Secondary omission: a random (not dev-selected) fixed prefix. A3(7) is chosen by a search over the bank for highest mean dev retrieval score, while A1(7)'s only dev tuning is scalar k*; a null A1-A3 is therefore partly explained by A3 being an optimized baseline rather than by conditioning being inert, and a random-7 arm would separate 'format alone suffices' from 'dev-selected items suffice'.
reviews.preprint_collision: The check is above average in form — nine queries, two named material collisions, an explicit scoop-exposure statement for Atlas, and a gap statement scoped as a claim about the search rather than proof of absence. It is undermined by its own audit trail: it reports that a previous round's citations (MemHarness 2607.28272, RecMem 2605.16045, AtomicRAG 2604.20844, Distractor-Aware Truncation 2608.03297, and 'Decocted Experience' 2604.04373, previously called the closest threat) could not be re-found, and that arXiv:2606.06036 appeared in the prior round under a different title. The same identifier carrying two titles across rounds is evidence that part of the reference set is confabulated, and the author further concedes Atlas's venue and authorship could not be verified beyond a returned introduction. Since novelty here rests entirely on 'no one runs this control', an unverifiable corpus is a substantive weakness, not a neutral: the two papers most likely to already contain a version of the control (Dynamic Cheatsheet 2504.07952, which maintains one shared cheatsheet, and ExpeL's own published insights-vs-trajectories ablation) are dismissed in a sentence each without reporting what their ablation tables actually contain at matched token budget. I would require the collision check to be re-run against verifiable listings and to state, per candidate, whether a fixed-set-vs-per-query arm at equal tokens exists.
